root_and_replay.root_purpose: The one interleaved paired root call computes both actual/reference native endpoints and saves the32 layer inputs plus final-norm input on CPU. It does not retain all native projections, MLP outputs or FA/FLA intermediates.
root_and_replay.replay_purpose: Reverse layer replay restores each saved paired layer input, runs that original native layer under actual capture contexts once, and supplies the actual endpoint operands to the unchanged finite decoder. Each layer is released after its finite consumer.
root_and_replay.checkpoint_comparison: This is a compute-for-memory recomputation strategy serving the same purpose as activation checkpointing in the actor. It is a manually scheduled no-grad finite-capture replay, not a second actor backward or attribution request. In the actual actor, the official activation_offload.py:538-544 disables the earlier HF checkpoint wrapper before installing its own checkpointed activation-offload wrapper. Thus fsdp_workers.py:268-269 alone is not the effective final checkpoint implementation, and two forward executions do not by themselves prove removable waste.
root_and_replay.boundary_of_necessity: The finite rules require correct paired endpoint operands. Obtaining them by replay is a current scheduling choice, not a mathematical requirement to execute a layer twice. Avoiding replay requires retaining or transporting the actual root operands at acceptable measured cost; current root checkpoints alone do not contain them.
root_and_replay.parameter_reuse: Current owner already retains each replayed layer's gathered weights until its finite consumer. The separate fsdp-parameter-owner-review receipt found67 all-gathers and zero collectives in the32 prepare calls, so there is no evidenced third layer gather to remove.

cross_response_reuse.already_shared: Current producer-workload review binds active lease lines22-40/60-82: longest literal canonical prompt once per UID, one native capture per padded canonical B4, disjoint state extraction segments, fresh owner HF cache leased to every consumer. Runner:229-256 duplicates/forks this unchanged factual cache for the paired suffix. Historical states before the common64-token cut are already shared.
cross_response_reuse.different_interventions: Readout:192-228,277-287 constructs each response's prompt + current actions + step-conditioned return query + single observed label. Reference replaces only that response's current action span with EOS. A prior action belongs to factual state for a later response; the later reference does not delete that prior action. The later prompt also contains newly observed state, and its query occurs at another causal predictor position. Those endpoint pairs are not interchangeable even if their scalar observed return is equal.
cross_response_reuse.factual_cache_limit: A canonical factual prefix can contain earlier actions, but NativePrefixArtifacts exports FA KV and boundary convolution/recurrent states, not the per-layer paired root/checkpoint or finite operands. The current paired ABI has one common suffix extent/cache boundary for both endpoints. No current callable seam accepts separate factual/reference prefix lengths or substitutes one canonical factual operand stream for paired replay.
cross_response_reuse.root_readout_methods: Runner:159-185 forward_prefix/read_outcomes expose native cached evaluation, but do not return the captured operands or a signed token attribution. Substituting these for attribute would drop required finite computation.
cross_response_reuse.remaining_common_cut_overhead: Already quantified elsewhere. The frozen88-request alternative aligned-prefix/context ordering improves combined suffix slots only1.58% and worsens rank1; source-start ordering increases work3.76%. No large speed claim or reordered production path follows from this audit.

multi_target_interface.actual_contract: PackedAnswerTargets supports several selected target offsets for the same endpoint pair and several independent samples in one batch. FiniteAnswerOps scatters their hidden seeds into one[sample,sequence,hidden] tensor. The runner propagates that tensor once and returns one[sample,sequence] signed vector. It has no separate target/query axis in its returned attribution.
multi_target_interface.not_a_reuse_seam_for_this_workload: Packing several offsets on one pair would form a combined objective, not independent per-query token vectors. Different response queries also do not share the same endpoint pair. Duplicating pairs as samples preserves identity but still executes them as samples, which the existing B4 interface already does. PLAN requires one full-return target/vector per response and forbids merged target seeds.
multi_target_interface.future_conditioning: Placing earlier queries into a final canonical trajectory or a single later sequence would change their factual causal prefix by exposing future observations/actions or preceding query/target tokens. This is outside the accepted target construction and is not proposed.

existing_capture_reuse_evidence.usable_owner_boundary: The only demonstrated capture-reuse seam is the native root layer's actual capture lifetime followed by its original reverse finite consumer. It can remove replay without inventing finite mathematics, as the historical candidate demonstrated, but no current ready-to-use schedule has both representative capacity and net wall-time evidence. This report does not propose another tape/loader/offloader.
existing_capture_reuse_evidence.evidence_needed_if_revisited: Preserve identical current actual IDs, EOS pairs, query/label, owner weights, cache state and finite calls. Compare actual consumed root/replay operands and dtypes with original operator references/assertions where affected; retain raw signed d/Q/V/A diagnostics without an invented whole-chain tolerance. Measure representative worst-real suffix plus exact32k B4 physical capacity and warmed end-to-end wall including capture/transport/cleanup against the current accepted path. An eliminated replay counter alone is insufficient.
